title: Cameron’s Cozy Apple Crumble Pie
description: A mix of tart Granny Smith, sweet red apples, and pear under a buttery cinnamon-oat walnut crumble, in a flaky pie crust.
imageAlt: Illustrated apple pie and slice with a golden cinnamon-oat crumb topping

source.name: Claire Saffitz’s pie recipe at Made In

items: ½ cup old-fashioned rolled oats (not quick cooking)
½ cup packed light brown sugar
10 tablespoons unsalted butter, chilled and cut into ½-inch pieces
1 frozen pie dough, thawed to room temperature (enough for one crust)
Cooking spray, for the pie pan
3 large red apples, such as Honeycrisp or Fuji (about 1½ pounds)
1 tablespoon fresh lemon juice (juice of about half a lemon)
½ teaspoon finely grated lemon zest
½ cup packed light brown sugar
2 tablespoons unsalted butter, chilled and cut into ½-inch pieces

steps.title: Make and chill the crumble
steps.text: Mix 1 cup flour, ½ cup oats, and ½ cup packed brown sugar in a bowl. Stir in 1 teaspoon cinnamon, ¼ teaspoon nutmeg, and ½ teaspoon kosher salt. Rub in 10 tablespoons chilled butter until no dry flour remains and the mixture clumps when squeezed. Stir in 1 cup chopped walnuts, cover, and refrigerate.
steps.why: Chilling firms up the butter again after mixing, helping the topping stay crisp and crumbly.

steps.title: Set up the oven
steps.text: Set a rack in the lower third and preheat to 425°F. Line a rimmed baking sheet with foil or a silicone mat.
steps.why: The lower rack helps the bottom crust brown. The lined sheet catches any juices that bubble over.

steps.title: Shape and freeze the crust
steps.text: Thaw the pie dough until soft and at room temperature. Lightly coat the pie dish with cooking spray and unroll the dough into it. Press it into the base and sides. Trim to a ½-inch overhang, fold it under, and crimp. Freeze uncovered while you prepare the filling.
steps.why: Thawed dough bends without cracking. Freezing the shaped crust firms it back up so the crimped edge holds its shape as it bakes.

steps.title: Slice and season the fruit
steps.text: Peel and core 6 small Granny Smith apples, 3 large red apples, and 2 firm pears. Cut about three-quarters into thin slices and the rest into ½-inch wedges. Toss with 1 tablespoon lemon juice and ½ teaspoon lemon zest, just enough to coat the fruit. Add ½ cup packed brown sugar, 3 tablespoons cornstarch, 2 teaspoons cinnamon, ¼ teaspoon nutmeg, and ½ teaspoon kosher salt. Toss until evenly coated.
steps.why: The thin slices soften into the filling and the wedges give it some texture. The lemon juice slows browning and balances the sweetness, the zest adds brightness, and cornstarch thickens the juices as the pie bakes.

steps.title: Fill the crust and add the crumble
steps.text: Pack about a quarter of the fruit across the bottom. Mound the rest and its juices in the center and press gently. Dot with 2 tablespoons chilled butter. Scatter the chilled crumble over the top, breaking up large clumps.
steps.why: Packing the fruit cuts down on gaps as it softens. Smaller crumble clumps crisp more evenly.

steps.title: Bake the pie
steps.text: Set the pie dish on the lined sheet. Bake at 425°F for 15 minutes. Lower the oven to 350°F and bake 60–75 minutes more, until the crust is golden and the filling bubbles. If the topping darkens early, loosely tent the center with foil.
steps.why: The initial high heat sets the crust. The lower temperature gives the fruit time to cook through and helps keep the crumble from burning.

steps.title: Cool the pie
steps.text: Transfer the pie to a wire rack and let it cool completely before cutting so the fruit filling has time to set.
steps.why: The filling sets as it cools, so it holds together when sliced.

notes.Choosing the fruit: Use 3 parts Granny Smith, 2 parts red apple, and 1 part pear. Granny Smith stays firm and tart, red apples add sweetness, and pears add softness and a mellow flavor. Today’s pie used 6 small Granny Smiths, 3 large red apples, and 2 pears, about 4 pounds before peeling. Keeping it simple? All Granny Smith is also very good.
notes.Make ahead: Store the cooled pie loosely covered at room temperature for up to four days. The crust is crispest on the first two days.
